input.quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use: (i) the Software, safely in executable object code format, at each AS400 at each of the Authorized Locations; and (ii) the Documentation.
input.rationale: Affiliate coverage is already built into the grant (affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, with no notice condition), and the licence is perpetual while fees are paid, so it is not revocable at will. However, the licence is expressly "non-transferable", Section 3(c) prohibits any transfer of the Work absent Garman's written authorization, and Section 20(d) requires consent for assignment of rights; there is therefore no path to carry the licence to a successor in a merger or acquisition. That fails the fallback element on a material term, so we have made the shortest change at fallback level: a successor transfer right in the grant without Garman's approval, with Section 3(c) conformed so no contradictory prohibition is retained. We have not touched the mutual assignment clause in Section 20(d), which we do not wish to loosen in Garman's favour.

mappings.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
mappings.quote: for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations

mappings.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.

proposal.summary: Add a right to transfer the licence to a successor by merger or acquisition without Garman's approval, and conform the Section 3(c) transfer prohibition.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Affiliate use is already covered, but the licence is expressly non-transferable and Section 3(c) bars any transfer without Garman's written authorization, so the licence would not survive a merger or sale of our business. We have added a successor transfer right by merger or acquisition without Garman's approval and conformed Section 3(c), which is our fallback position.
